cohorts.subjects: Living patients who had a spinal thoracic or abdominal CT, selected retrospectively from the hospital PACS; varied spinal problems (hernias and fractures named), only intact vertebrae above and below the problem area measured; excluded: implanted devices, visible osteoporotic deformation of the vertebral body, vertebrae with visible axial rotation relative to the scanner axis, spinal columns with a large lateral slant. Scanned supine. University Medical Center Groningen, the Netherlands (the acknowledgments thank its radiology department for the CT scans, p. 40). Ethnicity not stated. No statement on transitional or numbering anomalies.
cohorts.n_units: 12 endplates per spine region, T12 inferior to S1 superior; 25 measured per endplate as the stated goal, 10 points each, 3,000 coordinates in all (Inference: about 300 endplates from 77 patients, so each level comes from a different subset of patients)
cohorts.sexes: 46 male, 31 female; per-level sex counts not printed

techniques.instrument: Siemens 16-detector multi-detector CT (120 kV, 250 mAs, 0.75 s rotation, 16 x 0.75 mm collimation, 0.75 mm slices, 0.4 mm reconstruction index, B80s sharp kernel); read in Vitrea2 (Vital Images) on average intensity projections 3.13 mm thick
techniques.how: Three reference planes set in oblique mode with bone window: sagittal through the most anterior point of the body and the posterior niche, frontal through the most lateral points of the body, axial parallel to the endplate; measurement then in orthogonal mode. On the sagittal section a tangent line to the endplate is marked at equal distances and projected onto the endplate (points 1 to 5, 1 posterior rim, 5 anterior rim); the same on the frontal section (points 6 to 10, 6 right rim, 10 left rim). Bone edge at the largest drop in HU next to a manually located HU maximum (Waarsing's procedure). A least-squares plane through rim points 1, 5, 6 and 10; endplate depth is each point's perpendicular distance to it; sagittal diameter 1 to 5 and transverse diameter 6 to 10 (rim to rim); disc height between same-numbered points across a disc; wedge angle between adjacent endplate planes by Eijkelkamp's heights method. Levels T12 inferior to S1 superior; how T12 and S1 were identified is not stated.
techniques.magnification: not applicable: CT lengths in mm from the scanner calibration

techniques.instrument: the same CT settings as for the patients; maximum-gradient edge method
techniques.how: Outer superior and inferior sagittal and transverse endplate diameters, right and left body heights (points 6 to 6 and 10 to 10), anterior body height (5 to 5), spinous process length and transverse process width (repeatability); for the caliper comparison the four outer endplate diameters and the anterior and posterior body heights (5 to 5, 1 to 1). Best image plane chosen separately for each repeated measurement.

within_paper: The 77 patients are one pool: each of the 12 endplates was measured on 25 of them, and the paper says some vertebrae come from the same person, hence the mixed model (p. 36 (PDF 4)); which patients gave which levels is not printed. Figure 2 (all patients) and Table 2 (split by sex) are of the same patients (Inference: Table 2 is the sex split of the Figure 2 diameters, p. 37 and 39 (PDF 5 and 7)). The pig repeatability vertebra (one) and the caliper comparison vertebrae (two) are both measured by CT and caliper; whether the one is among the two is not stated (p. 36 (PDF 4)). No pig value is pooled with a human one.
